latin.280:
§. IV.
Ex eodem oppidò fundamentalium Christianae Religionis dogmatum eorundem Principio tàm Consensus Christianorum, quam Consociatio, id est tam Unitas mentis seu Spiritus, quam Unitas Corporis, seu Ecclesiae, dijudicanda.
latin.281: Secus, nec dabitur Consensus Christianorum catholicus ullus unquam, nec ulla Ecclesia Catholica, consensu istô copulata, ut & hanc frustra credamus & de istô mendaciter cantillemus: Die ganze Christenheit auf Erden / hält in einem Sinn gar eben.
latin.282: Nisi fortè, qui Orthodoxorum hodie nomine se jactitant, Catholicae quoque Ecclesiae titulum sibi solis quàm ridiculè vindicare, aut incogitanter ad se rapere attentent, utpote ne cum generibus quidem singulorum suorum, nedum cum singulis generum, quin ne cum uno quidem singulorum i. e. cum nemine ex suis secum ipsô, [admissâ locorum temporum aliorumque externorum, interna plurimùm mutantium, discriminatione ac mutatione] conciliandum.
latin.283: Unde porrò, uti jure meritoque Annot. superior. 2da consentientes in fide illos diximus, illosque solos, qui in Fundamentalibus omnibus consentiunt, in aliis licèt dissentiant; ita hôc locô omnes istos unam eandemque Ecclesiam Christianam constituere perhibemus, qui eadem Fundamentalia tenent.
latin.284: Quâ ratione Ecclesiasticâ Consociatione extorres arbitramur eos solos, qui in Fundamentalibus deficiunt, sive Theoreticis, quales sunt Sociniani, sive Practicis, quales sunt Pontificii, ad addititium suum fundamentum conscientias Christianorum quorumcumque, contra omnem charitatem Christianam, religioni Christianae quam maximè essentialem, sub anathematibus, obligantes.
latin.285: Vice versâ Protestantes Evangelicos, Reformatos atque Lutheranos, dissentientes licèt in nonnullis, ob Consensum tamen fundamentalem, eâdem jam tum Ecclesia Christiana contineri, Consociationeque Ecclesiasticâ copulatos esse: minimum hos, qui modos, quibus in tribus admodum dogmatibus quà Substantiam utriusque servatis, dissentiunt, fidei Christianae minus essentiales minusque fundamentales statuunt, eóque ab omni eatenus dissentientium damnatione non abstinent tantum, sed & abhorrent. De Arminianis strictè sic dictis jam pridem simile tulimus judicium, Inquis. in Armin. Annot. §. 1. 3.

pass_a.280: §. IV. From the same principle of the same fundamental dogmas of the Christian Religion both the Consensus of Christians and Consociation — that is, both Unity of mind or Spirit and Unity of Body or Church — are to be judged.
pass_a.281: Otherwise there will never be given any catholic Consensus of Christians, nor any Catholic Church coupled by that consensus — so that we would both believe this Church in vain and sing falsely of that consensus: “All Christendom on earth holds quite evenly in one mind.”
pass_a.282: Unless perhaps those who today boast themselves under the name of the Orthodox attempt — how ridiculously — to claim the title of the Catholic Church for themselves alone, or thoughtlessly to snatch it to themselves, seeing that they are not to be reconciled even with the kinds of their own individuals, still less with the individuals of the kinds, nay not even with one of the individuals — that is, with no one of their own with himself — [allowing for discrimination and change of places, times, and other externals that greatly alter internals].
pass_a.283: Whence further, as in the superior Annotation 2 we rightly and deservedly called those consenting in the faith, and those alone, who agree in all Fundamentals, though they dissent in others; so in this place we maintain that all those constitute one and the same Christian Church who hold the same Fundamentals.
pass_a.284: By which reckoning we judge exiles from Ecclesiastical Consociation only those who fail in the Fundamentals — whether Theoretical, such as the Socinians, or Practical, such as the Pontificians, binding under anathemas the consciences of any Christians whatever to their addititious foundation, against all Christian charity, which is most essential to the Christian religion.
pass_a.285: Conversely, Protestant Evangelicals, Reformed and Lutherans, though dissenting in some things, are already then contained in the same Christian Church and coupled by Ecclesiastical Consociation because of fundamental Consensus — at least those who judge the modes by which they dissent in about three dogmas (the Substance of both sides being kept) less essential and less fundamental to the Christian faith, and therefore not only abstain from but also abhor every damnation of dissenters so far. Concerning Arminians strictly so called we long ago rendered a like judgment, Inquiry into the Arminians, Annot. §. 1. 3.

280: §. IV. From that same principle of the Christian religion’s fundamental dogmas we must judge both Christians’ Consensus and their Consociation —
that is, both unity of mind (or Spirit) and unity of body (or Church).
281: Otherwise there will never be any catholic Christian consensus, nor any Catholic Church joined by that consensus.
Then we would believe that Church in vain, and sing falsely: “All Christendom on earth holds quite evenly in one mind.”
282: Unless those who today brandish the Orthodox name try — how ridiculously — to claim the Catholic Church’s title for themselves alone, or snatch it without thinking.
They cannot even be reconciled with the kinds among their own people, still less with each person in those kinds — not even with one individual, that is, with none of their own at one with himself —
once you allow for shifts of place, time, and other externals that greatly change internals.
283: So, as in Annotation 2 above we rightly called consenters in the faith only those who agree in all Fundamentals, though they differ elsewhere,
here we hold that all who keep the same Fundamentals make up one and the same Christian Church.
284: By that measure we count as exiles from church Consociation only those who fail in the Fundamentals —
theoretical failures such as the Socinians, or practical ones such as the Pontificians, who under anathemas bind any Christian conscience to their extra foundation,
against all Christian charity, which is most essential to the Christian religion.
285: Conversely, Evangelical Protestants — Reformed and Lutheran — though they dissent in some points, are already held in the same Christian Church and joined by church Consociation because of fundamental consensus.

At least those who treat the modes of dissent in about three dogmas (both sides keeping the substance) as less essential and less fundamental — and who not only refuse but abhor damning dissenters on that account.
On Arminians strictly so called we long ago gave a like judgment (Inquiry into the Arminians, Annot. §. 1. 3).
Stop before §. V (Hannekenius on truth and charity at the end of the Preliminary Questions).
